audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[].side read Ekko,Ekko,Ekko,Ekko,Ekko,Ekko,Skill while content win[] and the packet levelChart read Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Ekko,Ekko,Kassadin — a cross-layer disagreement on five of seven rows.
audit.why: Kit and win rate back the content layer: at 49.86% over 1039 games this is not a lane Ekko wins at every level, and Kassadin's Riftwalk drops from 5s to 2s at rank 3, which is the late-game flip the full layer denied.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side moved to Skill and phases[6].side to Kassadin, with those whys and ratings rewritten in the same group. win[] already holds the target values so no win[N] edit exists to pair.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] named a non-existent ability 'Riftslash'; spikes[3] referred to 'a completed Nether Blade item'.
audit.why: Kassadin's ultimate is Riftwalk and Nether Blade is his W, not an item.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around real names, the 40-mana Riftwalk cost with its escalating repeat cost, and the 2-second rank-3 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields (whys[6], spikes[3].text, content late, wants.foe[2]) claimed Riftwalk silences and 'shuts down your Chronobreak'. Riftwalk has no CC at all.
audit.why: Riot's text for Riftwalk is a blink that damages nearby units; the kit flags only 'dash'. The interrupt in Kassadin's kit belongs to Null Sphere (Q), which interrupts channels and shields him against magic damage — the interaction the page never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Silence claim removed everywhere and replaced with the real interactions: Null Sphere's magic shield absorbs your opener, Null Sphere interrupts channels, Void Stone reduces the magic damage your whole kit deals, and your Parallel Convergence stun cancels Null Sphere's channel.
sources: brief enemyKit P/Q/R text and flags

audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, and explicit sequencing added to dosFull[1].d and phases[3].why (trade into Force Pulse, commit once Null Sphere is spent).

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Even start: Q the wave and his toes from 1075, outside Null Sphere's 650, and the return pass pays for it.

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: E opens the blink-strike window, but Null Sphere shields the burst — bait the Q out, then Q-E-auto the third hit.

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: W zone games begin: its stun cancels Null Sphere's channel, so place it before you step in, not after.

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Even trades — Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1, so trade into it and leave before it charges again.

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive the carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Late Kassadin owns it: Riftwalk falls to 2s at rank 3, so he chains blinks faster than your 325-range E answers.

edits.before: Late game favors Kassadin outright since his scaled Riftwalk chains, magic resistance, and silence completely outclass Ekko's tools at equal gold.
edits.after: Late game favors Kassadin outright: a 2-second Riftwalk chains blinks and Void Stone's magic damage reduction blunts everything your kit does.

edits.before: Ekko's Chronobreak reset gives you a real edge over Kassadin's early Riftslash all-in since he's still mana-starved on his own ultimate, letting Ekko punish any overextension with a rewind before he scales into the matchup's real threat.
edits.after: Chronobreak gives you a real edge over Kassadin's early Riftwalk all-in: his ultimate costs 40 mana and each extra blink in a short window costs more, so punish every overextension with a rewind before he scales into the real threat.

edits.before: Late game Kassadin fully takes over the matchup — with a completed Nether Blade item and mana from Seraph's/Tear, he can chain 2-3 Riftwalks to burst and reposition faster than Ekko can react, and his silence on R shuts down your Chronobreak escape entirely.
edits.after: Late game Kassadin fully takes over — once his mana items are online he chains 2-3 Riftwalks on a 2-second cooldown to burst and reposition faster than Ekko reacts, while Null Sphere's shield eats your opener and Void Stone blunts the rest.

edits.before: Once Kassadin finishes his mana item and reaches late game, the matchup flips hard in his favor — his Riftwalk chains outpace your mobility, his magic resistance blunts your burst, and his R-silence can lock down your Chronobreak at the worst possible moment.
edits.after: Once Kassadin finishes his mana item and reaches late game, the matchup flips hard in his favor — Riftwalk on a 2-second cooldown outpaces your 325-range dash, Void Stone blunts your burst, and Null Sphere's magic shield absorbs the opener you needed to land.

edits.before: Time his ultimate's silence to shut down your Chronobreak the moment he all-ins
edits.after: Open with Null Sphere to shield the burst and interrupt anything you are channeling

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to the 2-second Riftwalk, then blinking onto you from an angle your E cannot answer.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Check it before every step-up. - R Chronobreak is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1 down to 2s at rank 3 — before that last rank the gaps are real, after it they are not. - Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and must charge. - Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1: fights, not waves.

edits.before: First item onward, trade like the rewind exists: dive the chipped, W the peel, R the answer. Your tempo compounds.
edits.after: The clock runs against you after first item — force fights before his mana item lands; Riftwalk at rank 2 is already 3.5s.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared push that crashes while your hologram bank stays healthy — tempo with insurance. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down — no blink, no string, no business being there. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-cleared push that crashes while your hologram bank stays healthy — deny him the CS his mana items need. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down — Riftwalk turns your walk home into a chase. Crash timing: crash early, while Riftwalk's gaps still exist and your dive still works.

edits.before: If Kassadin opens the score, reset expectations and respect Riftwalk doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q passes and stay relevant through W stuns and R picks.
edits.after: If Kassadin opens the score, stop dueling into Void Stone and farm with Q passes from 1075. Deny him the mana items — every wave he misses delays the 2-second Riftwalk that ends your lane.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry through insured dives — Chronobreak hits 50s at rank 3, and Kassadin caught mid-Riftwalk has no second exit.

edits.before: You are the pick that survives the response: dive their carry, Chronobreak the collapse, and W-stun the chase that follows you out.
edits.after: Late you are the pick, not the duelist: never meet Kassadin alone, W the blink line for your team, and Chronobreak out of his chain.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Place the anomaly on his blink line — the stun cancels Null Sphere and the shield never lands.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Wait until he spends Null Sphere and blinks in — Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1, so Chronobreak lands while he has no second escape.

edits.before: That is Kassadin’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: His 6 is a 5s blink, not burst — the coin-flip is yours to lose.

edits.before: The rewind heals off the hologram's path — diving away from your own past is how Ekkos die with R up.
edits.after: E is 325 range and 9s at rank 1 — greed in without the Q slow and Riftwalk simply leaves before you land.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Void Stone cuts the magic damage you deal and Null Sphere shields the rest — even HP in his wave is not even at all.

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3, and Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic burst — force the Q before you commit.
